>snippet 1: we prepare the dataset by loading and pruning the phylogeny, loading and matching the suture morphology data and the biological traits data, standardising and regressing suture complexity metrics by centroid size to account for allometric biases; from this point onwards, only scaled residuals will be used. Continuous biological predictors are also mathematically standardised, but not regressed with size variables. Necessary to run all that follows.

```{r, 1) dataset preparation for PMM}

# ============================================================
# Dataset preparation pipeline for PMM
# ============================================================

library(ape)
library(phytools)
library(MCMCglmm)

# -------------------------------
# Load phylogeny
# -------------------------------
tree <- read.tree("D:/Marco_backups/pipeline/4705sp_mean.nwk") # filepath for the tree
tree$tip.label <- gsub(" ", "_", tree$tip.label)

# -------------------------------
# Load suture-level measurements
# -------------------------------
data <- read.csv("D:/Marco_backups/pipeline/thrice_rescaled/complete_recast_metrics.csv", # file path for the complexity data set
                 stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
data$species <- gsub(" ", "_", data$species)

# -------------------------------
# Load species-level traits
# -------------------------------
species_traits <- read.csv("D:/Suppl_Mat/for_coauthors/Species_traits_sutures.csv", # file path for the biological trait data set
                               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
species_traits$species <- gsub(" ", "_", species_traits$species)

# -------------------------------
# Normalize species names
# -------------------------------
data$species <- tolower(data$species)
tree$tip.label <- tolower(tree$tip.label)
species_traits$species <- tolower(species_traits$species)

# -------------------------------
# Filter to species in tree
# -------------------------------
data <- data[data$species %in% tree$tip.label, ]

# Prune tree
pruned_tree <- keep.tip(tree, unique(data$species))

# Merge traits into suture-level dataset
data <- merge(data, species_traits, by = "species", all.x = TRUE)

# Create unique ID for each suture observation
data$suture_id <- paste(data$species, data$suture, sep = "_")



# -------------------------------
# Make tree ultrametric + inverse A matrix
# -------------------------------
library("dispRity")
# compute ages

recent<-pruned_tree$tip.label
ages <- tree.age(pruned_tree, digits = 10)

# make all recent tips extant
for(i in 1:length(recent)) {
  
  # get the tip
  this_tip <- recent[i]
  
  # if this tip is in the tree...
  if (this_tip %in% ages$elements) {
  
    # get the age
    this_age <- ages$age[ages$elements == this_tip]
    
    # get the new age
    new_age <- 0
    
    # get the old branch length
    tip_index <- which(pruned_tree$tip.label == this_tip)
    old_bl    <- pruned_tree$edge.length[pruned_tree$edge[,2] == tip_index]
    
    # compute the delta      
    delta <- new_age - this_age
    
    # compute the new branch length
    new_bl <- old_bl - delta
    
    # update the branch length
   pruned_tree$edge.length[pruned_tree$edge[,2] == tip_index] <- new_bl
    
  }
  
}


invA <- inverseA(pruned_tree, nodes = "TIPS", scale = TRUE)$Ainv
pruned_tree -> nu_tree

# Alignment sanity check
if (!all(unique(data$species) %in% rownames(invA))) {
  warning("Some species in data are not in the phylogenetic inverse matrix")
}


# -------------------------------
# Define variables
# -------------------------------
responses <- c("best_alpha","Convexity","Rugosity",
               "Sphericity","FD","centroid_size_mm")

predictors <- c("primary_diet","locomotion","habitat", 
                "suture","typical_lifespan","gestation_length", 
               "ln_body_mass_g","ln_brain_mass_g","weaning_age")

# -------------------------------
# Factor handling
# -------------------------------
factor_vars <- c("primary_diet","locomotion","habitat","suture")
factor_vars <- factor_vars[factor_vars %in% colnames(data)]
data[factor_vars] <- lapply(data[factor_vars], factor)

# -------------------------------
# Check predictors and responses exist
# -------------------------------
existing_predictors <- predictors[predictors %in% colnames(data)]
responses <- responses[responses %in% colnames(data)]

# Keep only complete rows for predictors
data <- data[complete.cases(data[, existing_predictors]), ]


# -------------------------------
# Create inverted complexity variables (1 / x), keep originals
# -------------------------------

invert_map <- c(
  best_alpha   = "alpha_complexity",
  Convexity    = "Concavity",
  Sphericity   = "Antisphericity"
)

invert_map <- invert_map[names(invert_map) %in% colnames(data)]

for (v in names(invert_map)) {
  new_var <- invert_map[[v]]
  
  # Safety check
  if (any(data[[v]] == 0, na.rm = TRUE)) {
    stop(paste("Zero values detected in", v, "- cannot invert safely."))
  }
  
  data[[new_var]] <- 1 / data[[v]]
}


# -------------------------------
# Scale continuous variables
# -------------------------------

cont_vars <- c(
  "best_alpha", "Convexity", "Rugosity",
  "Sphericity",  "FD", "centroid_size_mm",
  "typical_lifespan", "weaning_age",
  "gestation_length", "ln_body_mass_g", "ln_brain_mass_g",
  # NEW inverted variables
  "alpha_complexity", "Concavity", "Antisphericity"
)

cont_vars <- cont_vars[cont_vars %in% colnames(data)]
data[cont_vars] <- scale(data[cont_vars])

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Relative brain size
# ------------------------------------------------------------

data$rel_brain <- residuals(
  lm(ln_brain_mass_g ~ ln_body_mass_g, data = data)
)



# ============================================================
# Allometry significance + residual extraction
# ============================================================

allometry_vars <- c("alpha_complexity", "Concavity", "Antisphericity", "best_alpha", "Convexity", "Rugosity","Sphericity", "FD")

allometry_vars <- allometry_vars[allometry_vars %in% colnames(data)]

results_list <- list()

for (v in allometry_vars) {

  # Fit linear model for allometry
  model <- lm(data[[v]] ~ data$centroid_size_mm)

  # Add residuals to dataset
  data[[paste0(v, "_res")]] <- resid(model)

  # Extract statistics
  slope <- coef(summary(model))[2, 1]          # β1
  p_value <- coef(summary(model))[2, 4]        # p-value for β1
  r2 <- summary(model)$r.squared               # R²
  
  # Save results
  results_list[[v]] <- data.frame(
    variable = v,
    slope = slope,
    p_value = p_value,
    r_squared = r2
  )
}

# Combine into a single results table
allometry_results <- do.call(rbind, results_list)

# Show results
allometry_results




```

>snippet 2: we set up and run a first round of multi-response phylogenetic mixed models (MR-PMM) to assess the relationships between morphological variables; this is an intercept-only model without predictors, which allows us to assess the phylogenetic vs residual correlations among morphological variables. It also allows us to estimate phylogenetic signal of each morphological response variable.

```{r, 2) intercept-only MR(multi-response)-PMM + phylogenetic signal}
# ============================================================
# Intercept-only MR-PMM for phylogenetic vs residual correlations
# ============================================================

library(MCMCglmm)


#reframe scaled residuals as responses
responses <- c("alpha_complexity_res","Concavity_res","Rugosity_res",
               "Antisphericity_res","FD_res")

fit_intercept_only_model <- function(responses, data, nu_tree) {
  df <- data
  df <- df[complete.cases(df[, responses]), ]   # keep complete rows for all responses
  df$animal <- df$species
  
  # Prior for multi-response: residual + phylo covariance
  prior_multi <- list(
    R = list(V = diag(length(responses)), nu = length(responses) + 0.002),
    G = list(G1 = list(V = diag(length(responses)), nu = length(responses) + 0.002))
  )
  
  # Intercept-only fixed formula (~ 1)
  fixed_formula <- as.formula(
    paste("cbind(", paste(responses, collapse = ", "), ") ~ 1")
  )
  
  model <- MCMCglmm(
    fixed = fixed_formula,
    random = ~ us(trait):animal,   # phylogenetic covariance among traits
    rcov   = ~ us(trait):units,    # residual covariance among traits
    family = rep("gaussian", length(responses)),
    pedigree = nu_tree,
    data = df,
    prior = prior_multi,
    nitt = 80000, burnin = 20000, thin = 100,
    verbose = FALSE
  )
  
  return(model)
}

# -------------------------------
# Run intercept-only MR-PMM
# -------------------------------
intercept_model <- fit_intercept_only_model(
  responses = responses,
  data = data,
  nu_tree = nu_tree
)

par(mfrow=c(3,2), mar=c(2,2,1,0))
plot(intercept_model$Sol, auto.layout=F)


# -------------------------------
# Save full model for later reload
# -------------------------------
saveRDS(intercept_model, "Intercept_only_MRPMM_scaled_last.rds")


# -------------------------------
# Extract correlations
# -------------------------------

# Posterior means of (co)variance matrices
phylo_cov <- matrix(
  colMeans(intercept_model$VCV[, grep("animal", colnames(intercept_model$VCV))]),
  nrow = length(responses), byrow = TRUE
)
resid_cov <- matrix(
  colMeans(intercept_model$VCV[, grep("units", colnames(intercept_model$VCV))]),
  nrow = length(responses), byrow = TRUE
)

# Convert to correlations
phylo_cor <- cov2cor(phylo_cov)
resid_cor <- cov2cor(resid_cov)

# Add row/column names for clarity
rownames(phylo_cor) <- colnames(phylo_cor) <- responses
rownames(resid_cor) <- colnames(resid_cor) <- responses

# Save as CSVs
write.csv(phylo_cor, "Phylogenetic_correlations_scaled_last.csv", row.names = TRUE)
write.csv(resid_cor, "Residual_correlations_scaled_last.csv", row.names = TRUE)

# Print quick check
cat("\nPhylogenetic correlations:\n")
print(round(phylo_cor, 3))
cat("\nResidual correlations:\n")
print(round(resid_cor, 3))



# ============================================================
# Compute phylogenetic signal per trait from intercept-only MR-PMM
# ============================================================

compute_phylo_signal <- function(model, responses) {
  n_traits <- length(responses)
  
  # Extract variance components from posterior samples
  VCV <- model$VCV
  phylo_idx <- grep("animal", colnames(VCV))
  resid_idx <- grep("units", colnames(VCV))
  
  phylo_signal_results <- list()
  
  for (i in 1:n_traits) {
    # extract variance for this trait across MCMC samples
    phylo_var <- VCV[, phylo_idx[(i - 1) * n_traits + i]]
    resid_var <- VCV[, resid_idx[(i - 1) * n_traits + i]]
    
    h2 <- phylo_var / (phylo_var + resid_var)
    
    phylo_signal_results[[responses[i]]] <- data.frame(
      Trait = responses[i],
      Mean = mean(h2),
      LowerCI = quantile(h2, 0.025),
      UpperCI = quantile(h2, 0.975)
    )
  }
  
  phylo_signal_df <- do.call(rbind, phylo_signal_results)
  return(phylo_signal_df)
}

# -------------------------------
# Run signal computation
# -------------------------------
phylo_signal_df <- compute_phylo_signal(intercept_model, responses)

print(phylo_signal_df)
write.csv(phylo_signal_df, "Phylogenetic_signal_per_trait_scaled_last.csv", row.names = FALSE)


```

>snippet 3: setup to be able to run all further models - sets the base terms for data structure in the R environment. Necessary to run all that follows

```{r, 3) general model structure setup (default run)}

##running the SR model with size-corrected variables both for predictors and responses. Responses corrected by centroid size

# -------------------------------
# Define variables
# -------------------------------
responses <- c("alpha_complexity_res","Concavity_res","Rugosity_res",
               "Antisphericity_res","FD_res")

 
predictors <- c("suture", "primary_diet","locomotion","habitat",
                "typical_lifespan","gestation_length", 
                "ln_body_mass_g","rel_brain","weaning_age")

# -------------------------------
# Factor handling
# -------------------------------
factor_vars <- c("primary_diet","locomotion","habitat","suture")
factor_vars <- factor_vars[factor_vars %in% colnames(data)]
data[factor_vars] <- lapply(data[factor_vars], factor)

# -------------------------------
# Check predictors and responses exist
# -------------------------------
existing_predictors <- predictors[predictors %in% colnames(data)]
responses <- responses[responses %in% colnames(data)]

# Keep only complete rows for predictors
data <- data[complete.cases(data[, existing_predictors]), ]


# -------------------------------
# Make tree ultrametric + inverse A
# -------------------------------
library("dispRity")
# compute ages

recent<-pruned_tree$tip.label
ages <- tree.age(pruned_tree, digits = 10)

# make all recent tips extant
for(i in 1:length(recent)) {
  
  # get the tip
  this_tip <- recent[i]
  
  # if this tip is in the tree...
  if (this_tip %in% ages$elements) {
  
    # get the age
    this_age <- ages$age[ages$elements == this_tip]
    
    # get the new age
    new_age <- 0
    
    # get the old branch length
    tip_index <- which(pruned_tree$tip.label == this_tip)
    old_bl    <- pruned_tree$edge.length[pruned_tree$edge[,2] == tip_index]
    
    # compute the delta      
    delta <- new_age - this_age
    
    # compute the new branch length
    new_bl <- old_bl - delta
    
    # update the branch length
   pruned_tree$edge.length[pruned_tree$edge[,2] == tip_index] <- new_bl
    
  }
  
}


invA <- inverseA(pruned_tree, nodes = "TIPS", scale = TRUE)$Ainv
pruned_tree -> nu_tree

# Alignment sanity check
if (!all(unique(data$species) %in% rownames(invA))) {
  warning("Some species in data are not in the phylogenetic inverse matrix")
}

# -------------------------------
# Long format (optional, for univariate models)
# -------------------------------
long_data <- do.call(rbind, lapply(responses, function(trait) {
  df <- data[, c("suture_id", "species", existing_predictors)]
  df$trait_id <- trait
  df$response <- data[[trait]]
  return(df)
}))

long_data$trait_id <- factor(long_data$trait_id)
long_data$animal <- long_data$species
rownames(long_data) <- paste(long_data$suture_id, long_data$trait_id, sep = "_")

# Scale continuous predictors in long_data
cont_vars_long <- cont_vars[cont_vars %in% colnames(long_data)]
long_data[cont_vars_long] <- scale(long_data[cont_vars_long])

# -------------------------------
# Sanity check outputs
# -------------------------------
cat("Responses available:", paste(responses, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Predictors used:", paste(existing_predictors, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Data rows (wide):", nrow(data), "\n")
cat("Data rows (long):", nrow(long_data), "\n")

str(long_data)
str(data)

data$animal <- data$species


library(MCMCglmm)
library(combinat)  # for predictor combinations

get_predictor_combinations <- function(predictors, max_terms = 1) {
  combos <- list()
  for (i in 1:max_terms) {
    combos <- c(combos, combn(predictors, i, simplify = FALSE))
  }
  return(combos)
}



# -------------------------------
# Single-response (univariate) model selection
# -------------------------------

fit_single_response_models_fixed <- function(responses, data, predictors, nu_tree, max_predictors = 1) {
  df <- data
  df$animal <- df$species
  
  # Prior for univariate model: residual + phylo variance
  prior_uni <- list(
    R = list(V = 1, nu = 0.002),
    G = list(G1 = list(V = 1, nu = 0.002))
  )
  
  # Get all predictor combinations
  predictor_sets <- get_predictor_combinations(predictors, max_terms = max_predictors)
  
  all_results <- list()
  
  for (trait in responses) {
    cat("Running models for trait:", trait, "\n")
    
    df_trait <- df[complete.cases(df[, c(trait, predictors)]), ]
    
    trait_results <- list()
    
    for (pred_set in predictor_sets) {
      pred_str <- paste(pred_set, collapse = " + ")
      fixed_formula <- as.formula(paste(trait, "~", pred_str))
      
      tryCatch({
        model <- MCMCglmm(
          fixed = fixed_formula,
          random = ~ animal,          # phylogenetic effect
          rcov   = ~ units,           # residual
          family = "gaussian",
          pedigree = nu_tree,
          data = df_trait,
          prior = prior_uni,
          nitt = 80000, burnin = 20000, thin = 100,
          verbose = FALSE
        )
        
        trait_results[[pred_str]] <- list(
          model = model,
          DIC = model$DIC,
          predictors = pred_set,
          fixed_effects = summary(model)$solutions
        )
        
        cat("Finished model | Trait:", trait, "| Predictors:", pred_str, "| DIC:", model$DIC, "\n")
      }, error = function(e) {
        cat("Error fitting model for trait:", trait, "| Predictors:", pred_str, "\n")
      })
    }
    
    if (length(trait_results) > 0) {
      best_model <- trait_results[[which.min(sapply(trait_results, function(x) x$DIC))]]
      all_results[[trait]] <- list(
        all_models = trait_results,
        best_model = best_model,
        best_DIC = best_model$DIC,
        best_predictors = best_model$predictors
      )
    }
  }
  
  return(all_results)
}
```

>snippet 4: first round of single-response phylogenetic mixed models (SR-PMM) with suture as a fixed effect, testing all hypotheses as individual predictors. Predictors include biological traits (habitat, locomotion, diet, lifespan, gestation length, weaning age) and the classification of sutures within the dataset (suture identity).

```{r, 4) hypothesis testing with single predictors, suture as fixed effect}
library(MCMCglmm)
library(bayesplot)
library(stringr)


# ============================================================
# SETTINGS
# ============================================================

responses <- c(
  "Concavity_res",
  "Antisphericity_res",
  "FD_res",
  "alpha_complexity_res",
  "Rugosity_res"
)


predictors <- list(
  scale = "ln_body_mass_g",
  brain = "rel_brain",
  gest = "gestation_length",
  wean = "weaning_age",
  life = "typical_lifespan",
  diet = "primary_diet",
  locomotion = "locomotion",
  habitat = "habitat",
  suture= "suture"
)


 prior_uni <- list(
    R = list(V = 1, nu = 0.002),
    G = list(G1 = list(V = 1, nu = 0.002))
  )

# ============================================================
# MODEL FUNCTION
# ============================================================

run_model <- function(formula,data,tree){

  vars <- all.vars(formula)

  df <- data[complete.cases(data[,vars]),]

  m <- MCMCglmm(
    fixed=formula,
    random=~animal,
    rcov=~units,
    pedigree=tree,
    family="gaussian",
    data=df,
    prior=prior_uni,
    nitt=80000,
    burnin=20000,
    thin=100,
    verbose=FALSE
  )


  list(
    model=m,
    DIC=m$DIC,
    n_species=nrow(df),
    fixed_effects=summary(m)$solutions
  )
}




# ============================================================
#first model iteration
# ============================================================

rung0 <- list()

for(resp in responses){

  rung0[[resp]] <- list()

  # null model
  rung0[[resp]][["null"]] <-
    run_model(
      as.formula(
        paste(resp,"~1")
      ),
      data,
      nu_tree
    )


  # single predictor models
  for(nm in names(predictors)){

    f <- as.formula(
      paste(resp,"~",predictors[[nm]])
    )

    cat("Running",resp,nm,"\n")

    rung0[[resp]][[nm]] <-
      run_model(
        f,
        data,
        nu_tree
      )
  }
}

# ============================================================
# saving model RESULTS
# ============================================================


rung0_table <- do.call(rbind,lapply(names(rung0),function(resp){

  do.call(rbind,lapply(names(rung0[[resp]]),function(mn){

    x <- rung0[[resp]][[mn]]

    fe <- as.data.frame(x$fixed_effects)

    fe$predictor <- rownames(fe)

    rownames(fe)<-NULL


    colnames(fe)<-
      gsub("post.mean","estimate",
           colnames(fe))

    colnames(fe)<-
      gsub("l-95% CI","CI_lower",
           colnames(fe))

    colnames(fe)<-
      gsub("u-95% CI","CI_upper",
           colnames(fe))


    fe$response <- resp
    fe$model <- mn
    fe$DIC <- x$DIC

    fe

  }))

}))


write.csv(
  rung0_table,
  "rung0_all_predictors_suturefixed.csv",
  row.names=FALSE
)



# ============================================================
# SCREEN SUPPORTED PREDICTORS
# ============================================================


supported <- rung0_table[
  rung0_table$predictor!="(Intercept)" &
    (
      rung0_table$pMCMC <=0.05 |
      rung0_table$CI_lower>0 |
      rung0_table$CI_upper<0
    ),
]


# collapse categorical levels
supported$predictor <- sub(
  "(primary_diet|locomotion|habitat).*",
  "\\1",
  supported$predictor
)


selected_predictors <- unique(
  supported$predictor
)


print(selected_predictors)

```

>snippet 5: helper for visualising posterior differences among sutures (per complexity metric) for models with suture as a fixed effect

```{r, 5) visualising differences among sutures}
############################################################
# SUTURE STRUCTURE ANALYSIS PIPELINE
############################################################

library(tidyverse)
library("pheatmap")
library(FSA)
library(lme4)
library(performance)


############################################################
# 1. LOAD RESULTS
############################################################

results <- read.csv("Rung1_all_predictors_suturefixed.csv")


############################################################
# 2. EXTRACT SUTURE FIXED EFFECTS
############################################################

suture <- results %>%
  filter(model=="suture",
         predictor!="(Intercept)") %>%
  mutate(
    support = case_when(

      CI_lower > 0 | CI_upper < 0 &
      pMCMC < 0.05 ~ "supported",

      CI_lower > 0 | CI_upper < 0 ~ "CI only",

      pMCMC < 0.05 ~ "pMCMC only",

      TRUE ~ "none"
    )
  )


write.csv(
  suture,
  "suture_effects_summary.csv",
  row.names=FALSE
)



############################################################
# 3. SUTURE × COMPLEXITY HEATMAP
############################################################
library(pheatmap)

# Effect size matrix
heat <- suture %>%
  select(
    predictor,
    response,
    estimate
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = response,
    values_from = estimate
  ) %>%
  column_to_rownames("predictor")

rownames(heat) <- gsub("^suture", "", rownames(heat))

mat <- as.matrix(heat)


# Support matrix
support_mat <- suture %>%
  mutate(
    supported = support %in% c(TRUE, "Supported", "supported", 1)
  ) %>%
  select(
    predictor,
    response,
    supported
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = response,
    values_from = supported
  ) %>%
  column_to_rownames("predictor")

rownames(support_mat) <- gsub("^suture", "", rownames(support_mat))

support_mat <- as.matrix(support_mat)

# Replace TRUE/FALSE with symbols
symbols <- matrix(
  "",
  nrow = nrow(support_mat),
  ncol = ncol(support_mat)
)

symbols[support_mat == TRUE] <- "*"

pdf("suture_heatmap.pdf")
# Heatmap
pheatmap(
  mat,
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  cluster_cols = TRUE,
  display_numbers = symbols,
  number_color = "black",
  fontsize_number = 12,
  fontsize_row = 8,
  fontsize_col = 11,
  border_color = "grey80",
  main = "Suture-specific complexity\n* supported effect"
)

dev.off()

############################################################
# DEFINE SUTURE REGIONS DIRECTLY
############################################################

suture <- suture %>%
  mutate(
    suture_name = gsub("^suture", "", predictor),
    region = case_when(
      
      grepl("interpalatine|maxillarypalatine|sphenofrontal", suture_name) ~ 
        "basicranial",
      
      grepl("maxillary|premaxillary|nasal|jugal|temporozygomatic", 
            suture_name) ~ 
        "facial",
      
      grepl("frontal|sagittal|lambdoid|occipital|parietal|squamos", 
            suture_name) ~ 
        "cranial",
      
      TRUE ~ "other"
    )
  )


############################################################
# CHECK ASSIGNMENTS
############################################################

table(suture$region)

head(
  suture[,c("predictor","suture_name","region")]
)


############################################################
# KRUSKAL-WALLIS PER METRIC
############################################################

regional_tests <- suture %>%
  group_by(response) %>%
  summarise(
    KW = list(
      kruskal.test(
        estimate ~ region,
        data = pick(everything())
      )
    ),
    .groups="drop"
  )


regional_tests


############################################################
# DUNN POST-HOC TESTS
############################################################

suture %>%
  group_by(response) %>%
  group_walk(~{

    cat("\n\n", unique(.x$response), "\n")

    print(
      dunnTest(
        estimate ~ region,
        data=.x,
        method="bh"
      )
    )

  })
############################################################
# 7. VISUALISE REGIONAL EFFECTS
############################################################


ggplot(
regional,
aes(
region,
estimate
)
)+
geom_boxplot()+
facet_wrap(~response,
           scales="free")+
theme_bw()+
labs(
x="Anatomical region",
y="Suture effect estimate"

############################################################
# 8. RANDOM EFFECT VARIANCE EXPLAINED
############################################################

# assumes you saved your random effect models

# example:
# model <- Concavity_res ~ predictor + (1|suture)


variance_table <- data.frame()



for(m in names(random_models)){


x <- random_models[[m]]


vc <- as.data.frame(
VarCorr(x)
)


suture_var <-
vc %>%
filter(
grp=="suture"
) %>%
pull(vcov)


resid_var <-
vc %>%
filter(
grp=="Residual"
) %>%
pull(vcov)


ICC <-
suture_var /
(suture_var+resid_var)


variance_table <-
rbind(
variance_table,
data.frame(
metric=m,
suture_variance=suture_var,
residual_variance=resid_var,
ICC=ICC
)

)

}


variance_table


write.csv(
variance_table,
"suture_variance_explained.csv",
row.names=FALSE
)
```

>snippet 6: two-rung hypothesis testing with suture as a random effect - given that suture identity (var. name 'suture') is retrieved as being consistently and by far the strongest predictor of each suture morphology response variable (indicating that sutures are significantly different from each other), suture identity is recast as a random effect in addition to phylogenetic structure. This is to unbias further analyses from the effect of differences among sutures across skulls. 

>We run a first rung of analyses to individually test each of the competing hypotheses (predictors) for each separate complexity metric (response variable) (example structure: [response metric ~ predictor]). 

>For the second rung, we then run all the competing hypotheses that were supported in the first rung in a multi-predictor model, to identify independent effects that persisted after shared variance was accounted for (example structure: [response metric ~ predictor_1+predictor_2+predictor_3]).

```{r, 6) two-rung hypothesis testing}
library(MCMCglmm)
library(bayesplot)
library(stringr)


# ============================================================
# SETTINGS
# ============================================================

responses <- c(
  "Concavity_res",
  "Antisphericity_res",
  "FD_res",
  "alpha_complexity_res",
  "Rugosity_res"
)


predictors <- list(
  scale = "ln_body_mass_g",
  brain = "rel_brain",
  gest = "gestation_length",
  wean = "weaning_age",
  life = "typical_lifespan",
  diet = "primary_diet",
  locomotion = "locomotion",
  habitat = "habitat"
)


prior_uni <- list(
  R=list(V=1,nu=0.002),
  G=list(
    G1=list(V=1,nu=0.002),
    G2=list(V=1,nu=0.002)
  )
)



# ============================================================
# MODEL FUNCTION
# ============================================================

run_model <- function(formula,data,tree){

  vars <- all.vars(formula)

  df <- data[complete.cases(data[,vars]),]

  m <- MCMCglmm(
    fixed=formula,
    random=~animal+suture,
    rcov=~units,
    pedigree=tree,
    family="gaussian",
    data=df,
    prior=prior_uni,
    nitt=80000,
    burnin=20000,
    thin=100,
    verbose=FALSE
  )


  list(
    model=m,
    DIC=m$DIC,
    n_species=nrow(df),
    fixed_effects=summary(m)$solutions
  )
}




# ============================================================
# RUNG 1 INCLUDING NULL MODEL
# ============================================================

rung1 <- list()

for(resp in responses){

  rung1[[resp]] <- list()

  # null model
  rung1[[resp]][["null"]] <-
    run_model(
      as.formula(
        paste(resp,"~1")
      ),
      data,
      nu_tree
    )


  # single predictor models
  for(nm in names(predictors)){

    f <- as.formula(
      paste(resp,"~",predictors[[nm]])
    )

    cat("Running",resp,nm,"\n")

    rung1[[resp]][[nm]] <-
      run_model(
        f,
        data,
        nu_tree
      )
  }
}

# ============================================================
# SAVE RUNG 1 RESULTS
# ============================================================


rung1_table <- do.call(rbind,lapply(names(rung1),function(resp){

  do.call(rbind,lapply(names(rung1[[resp]]),function(mn){

    x <- rung1[[resp]][[mn]]

    fe <- as.data.frame(x$fixed_effects)

    fe$predictor <- rownames(fe)

    rownames(fe)<-NULL


    colnames(fe)<-
      gsub("post.mean","estimate",
           colnames(fe))

    colnames(fe)<-
      gsub("l-95% CI","CI_lower",
           colnames(fe))

    colnames(fe)<-
      gsub("u-95% CI","CI_upper",
           colnames(fe))


    fe$response <- resp
    fe$model <- mn
    fe$DIC <- x$DIC

    fe

  }))

}))


#write.csv(
 # rung1_table,
 # "Rung1_all_predictors.csv",
 # row.names=FALSE
#)



# ============================================================
# SCREEN SUPPORTED PREDICTORS
# ============================================================


supported <- rung1_table[
  rung1_table$predictor!="(Intercept)" &
    (
      rung1_table$pMCMC <=0.05 |
      rung1_table$CI_lower>0 |
      rung1_table$CI_upper<0
    ),
]


# collapse categorical levels
supported$predictor <- sub(
  "(primary_diet|locomotion|habitat).*",
  "\\1",
  supported$predictor
)


selected_predictors <- unique(
  supported$predictor
)


print(selected_predictors)



# ============================================================
# REMOVE BIOLOGICAL DUPLICATES
# ============================================================

# life history block
life_vars <- c(
  "gestation_length",
  "weaning_age",
  "typical_lifespan"
)


# keep only the strongest life history predictor
life_support <-
  supported[
    supported$predictor %in% life_vars,
  ]

if(nrow(life_support)>0){

  life_best <-
    life_support$predictor[
      which.min(life_support$CI_lower)
    ]

}else{

  life_best <- NULL

}


selected_predictors <-
  c(
    setdiff(selected_predictors,life_vars),
    life_best
  )


selected_predictors <- unique(
  selected_predictors
)


print(selected_predictors)



# ============================================================
# RUNG 2 MODELS
# ============================================================


rung2 <- list()


for(resp in responses){


  rhs <- paste(
    selected_predictors,
    collapse="+"
  )


  f <- as.formula(
    paste(resp,"~",rhs)
  )


  cat("Running higher model:",resp,"\n")


  rung2[[resp]] <-
    run_model(
      f,
      data,
      nu_tree
    )

}



# ============================================================
# SAVE RUNG 2 RESULTS
# ============================================================


rung2_table <- do.call(rbind,lapply(names(rung2),function(resp){

x <- rung2[[resp]]

fe <- as.data.frame(x$fixed_effects)

fe$predictor <- rownames(fe)

rownames(fe)<-NULL


colnames(fe)<-
gsub("post.mean","estimate",colnames(fe))

colnames(fe)<-
gsub("l-95% CI","CI_lower",colnames(fe))

colnames(fe)<-
gsub("u-95% CI","CI_upper",colnames(fe))


fe$response<-resp
fe$DIC<-x$DIC

fe

}))


#write.csv(
 # rung2_table,
 # "Rung2_higher_models.csv",
 # row.names=FALSE
#)



# ============================================================
# PLOTS
# ============================================================
library(ggplot2)
for(resp in names(rung2)){

  post <- as.matrix(
    rung2[[resp]]$model$Sol
  )

  post <- post[
    ,
    !colnames(post) %in% "(Intercept)",
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  if(ncol(post) > 0){

    colnames(post) <-
      str_wrap(colnames(post), 15)

    p <- mcmc_areas(
      post,
      prob = .95,
      prob_outer = .99,
      point_est = "mean"
    ) +
      ggtitle(resp)

    print(p)

    ggsave(
      filename = paste0("Rung2_", resp, ".pdf"),
      plot = p,
      width = 8,
      height = 6,
      units = "in"
    )

  }

}



install.packages("car")
vars <- c("ln_body_mass_g",
          "gestation_length",
          "weaning_age",
          "typical_lifespan",
          "rel_brain")

cor(data[, vars], use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

car::vif(lm(ln_body_mass_g ~ gestation_length +

                          rel_brain,
            data = data))
```

>snippet 7: helper for visualising supported models through sankey plots

```{r, 7) sankey for single-predictor models}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggsankeyfier)
library(tidyr)
library(scales)

############################################################
# LOAD DATA
############################################################

single <- read.csv(
  "D:/Suppl_Mat/script/data_analysis/Rung2_higher_models.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)


############################################################
# CLEAN
############################################################

single <- single %>%
  filter(
    predictor != "(Intercept)",
    pMCMC < 0.1
  )


############################################################
# COLLAPSE PREDICTOR CATEGORIES
############################################################

single <- single %>%
  mutate(

    predictor = case_when(

      # life history hypothesis
      predictor %in% c(
        "gestation_length",
        "weaning_age",
        "typical_lifespan"
      ) ~

        "gestation_length",


      # ecological predictors
      grepl(
        "^primary_diet",
        predictor
      ) ~

        "diet",


      grepl(
        "^locomotion",
        predictor
      ) ~

        "locomotion",


      grepl(
        "^habitat",
        predictor
      ) ~

        "habitat",


      TRUE ~

        predictor

    )

  )


############################################################
# RESPONSE LABELS
############################################################

single <- single %>%
  mutate(

    response = recode(

      response,

      "Antisphericity_res" = "Antisphericity",

      "Concavity_res" = "Concavity",

      "alpha_complexity_res" = "Alpha complexity",

      "FD_res" = "Fractal dimension",

      "Rugosity_res" = "Rugosity"

    )

  )


############################################################
# AGGREGATE
# one ribbon per predictor-response combination
############################################################

agg_df <- single %>%

  group_by(
    response,
    predictor
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    mean_effect = mean(
      estimate,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    abs_effect = mean(
      abs(estimate),
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    n = 1,

    .groups = "drop"

  ) %>%

  mutate(

    intensity = rescale(
      abs_effect,
      to=c(0.3,0.9)
    ),


    link_color = case_when(

      predictor %in% c(
        "diet",
        "locomotion",
        "habitat"
      ) ~

        alpha(
          "#00CCCC",
          intensity
        ),


      mean_effect > 0 ~

        alpha(
          "#6699FF",
          intensity
        ),


      mean_effect < 0 ~

        alpha(
          "#FF00FF",
          intensity
        ),


      TRUE ~

        alpha(
          "grey60",
          intensity
        )

    )

  )


############################################################
# SANKEY FORMAT
# predictor -> response
############################################################

sankey_data <- pivot_stages_longer(

  data = agg_df,

  stages_from = c(
    "predictor",
    "response"
  ),

  values_from = "n",

  additional_aes_from = "link_color"

)


############################################################
# NODE ORDER
############################################################

predictor_order <- c(

  "ln_body_mass_g",

  "rel_brain",

  "gestation_length",

  "diet",

  "locomotion",

  "habitat"

)


response_order <- c(

  "Antisphericity",

  "Concavity",

  "Alpha complexity",

  "Fractal dimension",

  "Rugosity"

)


############################################################
# APPLY ORDER
############################################################

sankey_data <- sankey_data %>%

  mutate(

    node = case_when(

      stage == "predictor" ~

        factor(
          node,
          levels=predictor_order
        ),


      stage == "response" ~

        factor(
          node,
          levels=response_order
        ),


      TRUE ~

        factor(node)

    )

  ) %>%

  arrange(
    stage,
    node
  )



############################################################
# POSITION
############################################################

pos <- position_sankey(

  v_space = 2,

  align = "justify",

  order = "as_is"

)



############################################################
# PLOT
############################################################

p <- ggplot(

  sankey_data,

  aes(

    x = stage,

    y = n,

    group = node,

    connector = connector,

    edge_id = edge_id,

    node_id = node

  )

) +

  geom_sankeyedge(

    aes(
      fill = link_color
    ),

    position = pos,

    alpha = 1

  ) +


  geom_sankeynode(

    position = pos,

    fill = "grey85",

    colour = "grey40"

  ) +


  geom_text(

    aes(

      label = node,

      hjust = after_stat(

        ifelse(
          connector=="from",
          -0.1,
          1.1
        )

      )

    ),

    stat="sankeynode",

    position=pos,

    size=3

  ) +


  scale_fill_identity() +


  scale_x_discrete(

    labels=c(

      predictor="Predictor",

      response="Response"

    ),

    expand=c(
      0.05,
      0.05
    )

  ) +


  labs(

    title="Single-predictor models",

    x=NULL,

    y=NULL

  ) +


  theme_minimal(

    base_size=12

  ) +


  theme(

    panel.grid=element_blank(),

    axis.text.y=element_blank(),

    axis.ticks=element_blank(),

    plot.title =
      element_text(
        face="bold",
        hjust=0.5
      )

  )



############################################################
# SAVE
############################################################

ggsave(

  "single_predictor_sankey_collapsed_competitive.pdf",

  plot=p,

  device=cairo_pdf,

  width=12,

  height=8

)


cat(
  "✅ Collapsed single-predictor Sankey saved\n"
)


```

>snippet 8: helper for extracting pairwise contrasts from the posterior distributions of the models (for categorical predictors)

```{r, 8) pairwise contrasts}
pairwise_global <- function(model, variable){

  post <- as.matrix(model$Sol)


  # find factor coefficients
  cols <- grep(
    paste0("^", variable),
    colnames(post),
    value = TRUE
  )


  if(length(cols)==0){
    return(NULL)
  }


  # reconstruct levels
  level_effects <- list()


  # reference level
  ref <- levels(data[[variable]])[1]

  level_effects[[ref]] <-
    rep(0, nrow(post))


  # add estimated contrasts
  for(i in seq_along(cols)){

    lev <- sub(
      paste0(variable),
      "",
      cols[i]
    )

    level_effects[[lev]] <-
      post[,cols[i]]

  }


  # pairwise comparisons

  comb <- combn(
    names(level_effects),
    2
  )


  results <- lapply(
    1:ncol(comb),
    function(i){


      a <- comb[1,i]
      b <- comb[2,i]


      diff <-
        level_effects[[a]] -
        level_effects[[b]]


      data.frame(

        comparison =
          paste(a,"-",b),

        estimate =
          mean(diff),

        CI_lower =
          quantile(diff,.025),

        CI_upper =
          quantile(diff,.975),

        P_positive =
          mean(diff>0)

      )

    })


  do.call(
    rbind,
    results
  )

}



library(ggplot2)


# ============================================================
# SETTINGS
# ============================================================

categorical_vars <- c(
  "primary_diet",
  "locomotion",
  "habitat"
)


dir.create(
  "pairwise_contrasts_plots",
  showWarnings = FALSE
)


# ============================================================
# LOOP THROUGH MODELS
# ============================================================

pairwise_results <- list()


for(resp in names(rung2)){


  cat("Processing:", resp, "\n")


  model <- rung2[[resp]]$model

  post <- as.matrix(model$Sol)


  for(var in categorical_vars){


    # check if predictor is in model

    if(!any(grepl(
      paste0("^",var),
      colnames(post)
    ))){
      next
    }


    cat("  ", var, "\n")


    # global pairwise contrasts

    pw <-
      pairwise_global(
        model,
        var
      )


    if(!is.null(pw)){


      # calculate Bayesian support

      pw$pMCMC <-
        2 * pmin(
          pw$P_positive,
          1 - pw$P_positive
        )


      pw$supported <-
        pw$pMCMC <= 0.05 |
        pw$CI_lower > 0 |
        pw$CI_upper < 0



      # add identifiers

      pw$response <- resp
      pw$predictor <- var


      pairwise_results[[
        paste(resp,var,sep="_")
      ]] <- pw



      # ----------------------------
      # PLOT
      # ----------------------------


      p <- ggplot(
        pw,
        aes(
          y=reorder(comparison,estimate),
          x=estimate,
          colour=supported
        )
      )+

        geom_vline(
          xintercept=0,
          linetype="dashed"
        )+

        geom_errorbarh(
          aes(
            xmin=CI_lower,
            xmax=CI_upper
          ),
          height=.2
        )+

        geom_point(
          size=3
        )+

        scale_colour_manual(
          values=c(
            "FALSE"="black",
            "TRUE"="red"
          )
        )+

        labs(
          title=paste(
            resp,
            "-",
            var
          ),
          x="Posterior difference",
          y=NULL,
          colour="Supported"
        )+

        theme_classic()



      ggsave(
        filename=paste0(
          "pairwise_contrasts_plots/",
          resp,
          "_",
          var,
          "_pairwise.pdf"
        ),
        plot=p,
        width=7,
        height=5
      )


    }

  }

}



# ============================================================
# EXPORT CSV
# ============================================================


pairwise_table <- do.call(
  rbind,
  pairwise_results
)


write.csv(
  pairwise_table,
  "Rung2_global_pairwise_contrasts.csv",
  row.names=FALSE
)
```

>snippet 9: helper for plotting rebalanced pairwise contrast results for categorical predictors (to be able to visualise the baseline intercept level)

```{r, 9) plotting with reference level rebalancing}
library(MCMCglmm)
library(bayesplot)
library(stringr)


# ============================================================
# SETTINGS
# ============================================================

dir.create(
  "Rung2_plots",
  showWarnings = FALSE
)


# Continuous variables in Rung 2
continuous_vars <- c(
  "ln_body_mass_g",
  "rel_brain",
  "gestation_length",
  "weaning_age",
  "typical_lifespan"
)


# ============================================================
# PLOT EACH RESPONSE
# ============================================================

for(resp in names(rung2)){


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # POSTERIOR SAMPLES
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  post <- as.matrix(
    rung2[[resp]]$model$Sol
  )


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # GET DATA USED FOR THIS MODEL
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  formula <- rung2[[resp]]$model$Fixed$formula

  vars <- all.vars(formula)

  df <- data[
    complete.cases(data[, vars]),
  ]


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # LIST TO STORE POSTERIOR DISTRIBUTIONS
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  plot_post <- list()


  # ==========================================================
  # CONTINUOUS PREDICTORS
  # ==========================================================

  for(v in continuous_vars){

    if(v %in% colnames(post)){

      plot_post[[v]] <- post[, v]

    }

  }


  # ==========================================================
  # CATEGORICAL PREDICTORS
  # ==========================================================


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # DIET
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  if("primary_diet" %in% vars){

    diet_levels <- levels(
      factor(df$primary_diet)
    )

    diet_ref <- diet_levels[1]


    # reference category
    plot_post[[paste0("Diet: ", diet_ref)]] <- post[, "(Intercept)"]


    # non-reference categories
    for(level in diet_levels[-1]){

      coefficient <- paste0(
        "primary_diet",
        level
      )

      if(coefficient %in% colnames(post)){

        plot_post[[paste0("Diet: ", level)]] <-post[, "(Intercept)"] +post[, coefficient]

      }

    }

  }


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # LOCOMOTION
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  if("locomotion" %in% vars){

    locomotion_levels <- levels(
      factor(df$locomotion)
    )

    locomotion_ref <- locomotion_levels[1]


    # reference category
    plot_post[[paste0("Locomotion: ",  locomotion_ref )]] <- post[, "(Intercept)"]


    # non-reference categories
    for(level in locomotion_levels[-1]){

      coefficient <- paste0(
        "locomotion",
        level
      )

      if(coefficient %in% colnames(post)){

        plot_post[[paste0("Locomotion: ",level)]] <-post[, "(Intercept)"] + post[, coefficient]

      }

    }

  }


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # HABITAT
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  if("habitat" %in% vars){

    habitat_levels <- levels(
      factor(df$habitat)
    )

    habitat_ref <- habitat_levels[1]


    # reference category
    plot_post[[paste0("Habitat: ",habitat_ref)]] <- post[, "(Intercept)"]


    # non-reference categories
    for(level in habitat_levels[-1]){

      coefficient <- paste0(
        "habitat",
        level
      )

      if(coefficient %in% colnames(post)){

        plot_post[[paste0( "Habitat: ",level)]] <- post[, "(Intercept)"] +post[, coefficient]

      }

    }

  }


  # ==========================================================
  # REMOVE INTERCEPT
  # ==========================================================

  # The intercept itself is no longer plotted because its
  # information has been incorporated into the categorical
  # level estimates above.

  plot_post[["(Intercept)"]] <- NULL


  # ==========================================================
  # CONVERT TO MATRIX
  # ==========================================================

  plot_post <- do.call(
    cbind,
    plot_post
  )


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # WRAP LABELS
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  colnames(plot_post) <-
    str_wrap(
      colnames(plot_post),
      20
    )


  # ==========================================================
  # PLOT
  # ==========================================================

  p <- mcmc_areas(
    plot_post,
    prob = .95,
    prob_outer = .99,
    point_est = "mean"
  ) +
    ggtitle(resp)


  print(p)


  # ==========================================================
  # SAVE PDF
  # ==========================================================

  safe_resp <- gsub(
    "[^A-Za-z0-9_-]",
    "_",
    resp
  )


  ggsave(
    filename = file.path(
      "Rung2_plots",
      paste0(
        "Rung2_",
        safe_resp,
        ".pdf"
      )
    ),
    plot = p,
    width = 9,
    height = 7,
    units = "in"
  )

}
```

>snippet 11: convergence testing on the final model design (single-responses, with sutures as a random effect). Run only after models (or a sample of models) have been already run, so that the data is already loaded in your environment. To save processing time, the process currently runs on the models with suture as a random effect, for significant effects. Change the input models to test convergence in different model structures used throughout.

```{r, 11) convergence testing and diagnostics for individual model suitability}

# ============================================================
# RUN SELECTED MODELS FROM CSV WITH 2 CHAINS + GELMAN-RUBIN
# ============================================================

library(MCMCglmm)
library(coda)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. PRIOR
# ------------------------------------------------------------
prior_uni <- list(
  R = list(V = 1, nu = 0.002),
  G = list(
    G1 = list(V = 1, nu = 0.002),
    G2 = list(V = 1, nu = 0.002)
  )
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. READ CSV + REMOVE DUPLICATES
# ------------------------------------------------------------
df_models <- read.csv("D:/Suppl_Mat/script/data_analysis/Rung1_curated.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
df_models <- unique(df_models[, c("trait", "predictor")])

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. BUILD FORMULA FUNCTION
# ------------------------------------------------------------
build_formula <- function(trait, predictors_string) {
  preds <- unlist(strsplit(predictors_string, ","))
  preds <- trimws(preds)
  as.formula(paste(trait, "~", paste(preds, collapse = " + ")))
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. RUN MODELS (2 CHAINS EACH)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
results <- list()

for (i in seq_len(nrow(df_models))) {
  
  trait <- df_models$trait[i]
  preds <- df_models$predictor[i]
  
  f <- build_formula(trait, preds)
  name <- paste(trait, preds, sep = "_")
  
  cat("\n=============================================\n")
  cat("Running:", name, "\nFormula:", deparse(f), "\n")
  cat("=============================================\n")
  
  # subset data
  vars <- all.vars(f)
  df_sub <- data[complete.cases(data[, vars]), ]
  
  # ---------------------------
  # RUN TWO CHAINS
  # ---------------------------
  
  model1 <- MCMCglmm(
    fixed = f,
    random = ~ animal + suture,
    rcov = ~ units,
    family = "gaussian",
    pedigree = nu_tree,
    data = df_sub,
    prior = prior_uni,
    nitt = 80000, burnin = 20000, thin = 100,
    verbose = FALSE
  )
  
  model2 <- MCMCglmm(
    fixed = f,
    random = ~ animal + suture,
    rcov = ~ units,
    family = "gaussian",
    pedigree = nu_tree,
    data = df_sub,
    prior = prior_uni,
    nitt = 80000, burnin = 20000, thin = 100,
    verbose = FALSE
  )
  
  # ---------------------------
  # COMBINE CHAINS
  # ---------------------------
  
  chains <- mcmc.list(model1$Sol, model2$Sol)
  
  # ---------------------------
  # GELMAN-RUBIN
  # ---------------------------
  
  gr <- gelman.diag(chains, multivariate = FALSE)
  converged <- all(gr$psrf[,1] < 1.1)
  
  # ---------------------------
  # STORE RESULTS
  # ---------------------------
  
  results[[name]] <- list(
    formula = f,
    model_chain1 = model1,
    model_chain2 = model2,
    DIC = mean(c(model1$DIC, model2$DIC)),
    gelman_rubin = gr,
    converged = converged
  )
  
  cat("Finished:", name,
      "| mean DIC =", round(results[[name]]$DIC, 2),
      "| converged =", converged, "\n")
  
  # optional save per model
  # saveRDS(results[[name]], file = paste0("models/", name, ".rds"))
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. LIST NON-CONVERGED MODELS
# ------------------------------------------------------------
bad_models <- names(results)[!sapply(results, function(x) x$converged)]

cat("\n=============================\n")
cat("Non-converged models:\n")
print(bad_models)
cat("=============================\n")


summary_list <- list()

for (name in names(results)) {
  
  gr <- results[[name]]$gelman_rubin$psrf
  
  df <- data.frame(
    model = name,
    parameter = rownames(gr),
    Rhat = gr[,1],
    upper_CI = gr[,2],
    converged = gr[,1] < 1.1
  )
  
  summary_list[[name]] <- df
}

summary_df <- do.call(rbind, summary_list)

write.csv(summary_df, "D:/Suppl_Mat/script/data_analysis/gelman_rubin_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)

model_summary <- data.frame(
  model = names(results),
  max_Rhat = sapply(results, function(x) max(x$gelman_rubin$psrf[,1])),
  mean_Rhat = sapply(results, function(x) mean(x$gelman_rubin$psrf[,1])),
  converged = sapply(results, function(x) all(x$gelman_rubin$psrf[,1] < 1.1)),
  DIC = sapply(results, function(x) x$DIC)
)

write.csv(model_summary, "D:/Suppl_Mat/script/data_analysis/model_structure_testing.csv", row.names = FALSE)

out_dir <- "D:/Suppl_Mat/script/data_analysis/gelman_plots/"

if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE)

for (name in names(results)) {
  
  # clean filename (important if names contain special characters)
  safe_name <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9_]", "_", name)
  
  file_path <- file.path(out_dir, paste0("gelman_", safe_name, ".pdf"))
  
  pdf(file_path, width = 6, height = 6)
  
  chains <- mcmc.list(
    results[[name]]$model_chain1$Sol,
    results[[name]]$model_chain2$Sol
  )
  
  gelman.plot(chains)
  title(main = name)
  
  dev.off()
}

library(coda)


out_dir <- "D:/Suppl_Mat/script/data_analysis/trace_plots/"
if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE)

library(coda)

for (name in names(results)) {
  
  safe_name <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9_]", "_", name)
  file_path <- file.path(out_dir, paste0("trace_", safe_name, ".pdf"))
  
  pdf(file_path, width = 14, height = 8)
  
  # combine both chains
  chains <- mcmc.list(
    results[[name]]$model_chain1$Sol,
    results[[name]]$model_chain2$Sol
  )
  
  par(mfrow = c(2,2), mar = c(2, 1, 2, 1))
  plot(chains, ask = FALSE, auto.layout = FALSE)
  title(main = name)
  
  dev.off()
}

```

>snippet 12: helper to generate a PCA of suture mean values and extract PCA loadings

```{r, 12) generate PCA plot}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)

# ================================
# 1. Variable selection
# ================================
all_resp_vars <- c(
   "Concavity_res", 
  "Antisphericity_res", "FD_res", "Rugosity_res","alpha_complexity_res")

all_resp_vars <- all_resp_vars[all_resp_vars %in% colnames(data)]

size_vars <- c("HeightRange", "Planar", "centroid_size_mm", "actual_volume")

resp_vars_nosize <- setdiff(all_resp_vars, size_vars)

# Dataset 
df_res <- data %>%
  select(all_of(resp_vars_nosize), suture)



# ================================
# 4. PCA on residuals
# ================================
pca_res <- prcomp(df_res %>% select(all_of(resp_vars_nosize)),
                  center = TRUE, scale. = FALSE)

#pca_res$x[, "PC1"]    <- -pca_res$x[, "PC1"]
#pca_res$rotation[, "PC1"] <- -pca_res$rotation[, "PC1"]

pca_res$x[, "PC2"]    <- -pca_res$x[, "PC2"]
pca_res$rotation[, "PC2"] <- -pca_res$rotation[, "PC2"]


eigen_res <- pca_res$sdev^2
prop_res  <- eigen_res / sum(eigen_res)




suture_regions <- data.frame(
  suture = c(
    "coronal", "frontojugal", "frontomaxillary", "frontonasal",
    "frontopremaxillary", "interfrontal", "internasal", "interpalatine",
    "lambdoid", "maxillaryjugal", "maxillarypalatine", "maxillarypremaxillary",
    "nasomaxillary", "nasopremaxillary", "occipital", "occipitoparietal",
    "sagittal", "sphenofrontal", "squamosalparietal", "squamosooccipital",
    "temporozygomatic"
  ),
  Region = c(
    "Neurocranial", "Transitional", "Transitional", "Transitional",
    "Transitional", "Neurocranial", "Viscerocranial", "Viscerocranial",
    "Neurocranial", "Viscerocranial", "Viscerocranial", "Viscerocranial",
    "Viscerocranial", "Viscerocranial", "Neurocranial", "Neurocranial",
    "Neurocranial", "Neurocranial", "Neurocranial", "Neurocranial",
    "Transitional"
  )
)
# ================================
# 5. Scores and suture means
# ================================
scores_res <- as.data.frame(pca_res$x) %>%
  mutate(suture = df_res$suture)

means_res <- scores_res %>%
  group_by(suture) %>%
  summarise(across(starts_with("PC"), mean))



# Add Region information
means_res <- means_res %>%
  left_join(suture_regions, by = c("suture" = "suture"))


# ================================
# 6. Region convex hulls
# ================================
region_hulls_res <- means_res %>%
  group_by(Region) %>%
  slice(chull(PC1, PC2)) %>%
  ungroup()


# ================================
# 7. Loadings (arrows)
# ================================
load_res <- as.data.frame(pca_res$rotation[,1:3])
load_res$var <- rownames(load_res)


mult_res <- 0.6 * min(
  diff(range(means_res$PC1)) / diff(range(load_res$PC1)),
  diff(range(means_res$PC2)) / diff(range(load_res$PC2))
)

load_res <- load_res %>%
  mutate(arrow_x = PC1 * mult_res,
         arrow_y = PC2 * mult_res)


# ================================
# 8. Plot PCA
# ================================


p_res <- 
  pdf("PCA_sutures_last_new.pdf", width = 7, height = 5)
  ggplot(means_res, aes(PC1, PC2)) +
  geom_polygon(data = region_hulls_res,
               aes(fill = Region, group = Region),
               alpha = 0.25, color = NA) +
  geom_point(aes(color = Region), size = 4, shape = 21, stroke = 0.4) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = suture, color = Region),
                  size = 4, fontface = "bold", show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_segment(data = load_res,
               aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = arrow_x, yend = arrow_y),
               inherit.aes = FALSE,
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.02, "npc"))) +
  geom_text_repel(data = load_res,
                  aes(x = arrow_x, y = arrow_y, label = var),
                  inherit.aes = FALSE,
                  size = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "PCA on Residuals (Regressed on Scaled Centroid Size)",
    subtitle = "best_alpha, Convexity, Sphericity inverted; region-level convex hulls",
    x = paste0("PC1 (", round(prop_res[1] * 100, 1), "%)"),
    y = paste0("PC2 (", round(prop_res[2] * 100, 1), "%)")
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

dev.off()

pca_res$rotation[,1:3]
prop_res[1] * 100
prop_res[2] * 100
prop_res[3] * 100

sapply(df_res[resp_vars_nosize], var)
```
